title: adjacent-fit-lens-hector-ibarra
content:
Quick frame: informal, jotting impressions through an "adjacent-fit" lens — i.e., not just strict job-skill mapping but how the candidate would slot into adjacent areas we care about (oncall culture, infra/product partnerships, ambiguity tolerance). Use as a supplement to the formal scorecard.

Candidate snapshot
- Name: Maya Khalil (candidate folder: maya-khalil-runtime)
- Loop date: 2024-09-17
- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference serving)
- Interviewers: Hector Ibarra (me), Priya Nair (SRE), Ari Morales (ML infra)
- Recruiter notes: strong LLM infra background at prior company, mostly kubernetes/GPU infra, authored two internal tools for batching & KV cache visibility.

High-level gut
- Energetic, iterative problem-solver. Tends to prototype quickly to validate assumptions (good for our fast turnaround on model rollouts).
- Comfortable with messy ops and cross-team tradeoffs (latency vs cost), but less opinionated about long-term API/SDK ergonomics (could be paired with devexp folks).
- Would likely thrive on Dedicated/Private workstreams where we need pragmatic infra ownership + customer-facing debugging.

Strengths observed
- Pragmatic debugging: walked through a degraded-throughput scenario and rapidly isolated a KV cache eviction issue, proposing a local reproduction (mini-benchmark) and a fix (write-through cache + metrics).
- Systems mental model: clear on kernel/hw mismatch tradeoffs (quantization, memory-bound vs compute-bound) and how that affects batching strategy.
- Shipping bias: gave concrete examples of rolling fixes to infra in production, including rollback/playbook design.

Concerns / open questions
- Scale mental model at RL/inference p99: she has good hands-on experience up to mid-sized fleets; unclear on multi-tenant QoS at 100s of concurrent long-lived chat sessions. Might need incubated exposure to extreme SLOs.
- API-first thinking: less concrete thoughts on SDK design or developer ergonomics; may defer to product teams rather than drive them.
- Leadership scope: strong IC with occasional tech-lead instincts; ambiguous on whether she wants people management or to remain deep IC. Clarify in follow-up.

Key behavioral notes (quotes & moments)
- On ambiguity: "I like building a small failing test that tells me whether the hypothesis is even in the right ballpark" — repeated theme of test-driven exploration.
- On tradeoffs: emphasized minimizing blast radius over micro-optimizations until metrics are stable. Good risk-first instincts.
- On cross-team work: described a time she negotiated rolling windows and throttles with product, showing diplomacy.

Technical probes + candidate answers (bulleted)
- Problem: design a fallback when top-tier GPU pool saturates.
  - Candidate approach: prioritize policy routing by request class -> short-circuit to quantized variant or lower-capacity region -> degrade features gracefully (e.g., cap context length) -> alerting + canary for correctness. Specifics: use per-token cost signal + SLA tag to route.
  - My notes: realistic and operational; would like to see more on safety/QA gating for lower-precision models.

- Problem: debugging p99 latency spikes that correlate with KV cache misses.
  - Candidate approach: capture trace spans on cache hit/miss, add histograms per model-variant, run compaction tests, add predictive prefetching for hot prefixes.
  - My notes: good telemetry-first approach; prefetch idea practical but need to see cost-control constraints.

- Deep dive: explain attention memory growth for long chat sessions and mitigation strategies.
  - Candidate discussed kv-cache sharding, checkpointing, and chunked attention; suggested async eviction + state-on-disk for cold sessions.
  - My notes: shows good awareness of memory/IO tradeoffs for on-demand long-horizon sessions.

Quantitative quick-scan (out of 10, rough)
- System design: 8
- Debugging & triage: 9
- Performance mindset (latency/cost): 8
- Cross-team communication: 7
- Product/SDK sensibilities: 5
- Overall: 8 (strong IC, low risk)

Recommendation (short)
- Move to onsight pairing (2–3 hour pairing with an infra engineer focused on multi-tenant QoS). Candidate likely passes for Senior role; if we need someone to drive SDK/product, flag that for hire plan or pair with devexp.

Suggested next steps / action items
- Schedule technical pairing with Diego Ramos (SLO/QoS) and Priya for oncall expectations.
- Ask recruiter to clarify candidate preference for IC vs manager and willingness to own customer-facing incidents.
- Small take-home: reproduce a KV-cache miss pattern and propose a low-risk rollout plan (2–3 day task). This helps us see thoughtfulness around rollout safety.

Notes to hiring committee (explicit asks)
- If moving forward, consider compensation leaning slightly higher for demonstrated production ownership and GPU infra familiarity (benchmarked against INF hires in Q2).
- If we want a devexp-heavy Senior, add a follow-up with product/devexp to probe SDK/UX-oriented instincts.

Loose links & references (for internal follow-up)
- Related GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/719 (batching changes we referenced)
- Perf replay ticket: JIRA INF-4821 (repro KV-cache flake)
- Slack thread: #runtime-incidents (link: slack.com/archives/G0123456)

Personal reflection / meta-notes for me
- Felt like a high-quality IC candidate who will deliver value quickly in Dedicated/Private contexts. Worth investing a short pairing rather than immediate pass/fail.
- Useful signal: she focused on testable experiments rather than long speculative designs — aligns with our prefer-to-iterate culture.

-- end of scratchpad (not polished) --

Action log: Hector to create pairing calendar invite + follow-up with recruiter by 2024-09-21.
